records.title: Homo sapiens-specific evolution unveiled by ancient southern African genomes
records.sample_size_raw: Genomic and radiocarbon data from 28 ancient individuals from South Africa were analysed in this study. The sample size was dependent on the availability of human remains dating to the Stone Age and Iron Age from southern Africa, with preserved and retrievable ancient DNA sequences. These specimens are very rare, given the poor molecular preservation of human remains from this period in that region. Given the millions of genetic variants analysed for each individual, information about the genetic history can be retrieved.

records.title: Uncovering the role of LINE-1 in the evolution of lung adenocarcinoma
records.sample_size_raw: We analyzed deep whole-genome sequencing (mean read depth 81.7x) and multi-omics data from 1,024 LUAD samples in the Sherlock-Lung study, collected from multiple centers across four continents. This large and diverse cohort included 286 smokers, 737 never-smokers, and 1 participant with unknown smoking status, providing broad representation of key etiologic subgroups. To ensure robust statistical power for identifying subclonal architectures and reconstructing lung cancer evolutionary histories, we applied the number of reads per tumor chromosomal copy (NRPCC) metric to evaluate sequencing depth in relation to tumor ploidy. Based on stringent quality control criteria (NRPCC > 10, purity > 0.3, and reliable copy-number profiling), we selected 542 LUAD tumors for downstream clonal evolution analyses. These thresholds ensured that each tumor had sufficient coverage and signal-to-noise ratio for accurate detection of clonal and subclonal events, thereby providing a statistically well-powered dataset to support evolutionary inference and subgroup comparisons.
